'''Attila Grandpierre''' ({{langx|hu|Grandpierre Attila}}; born 4 July 1951) is a Hungarian musician, [[astrophysicist]], physicist, self-taught historian, writer and poet. He is best known as leader/vocalist of the [[Galloping Coroners]] ({{langx|hu|Vágtázó Halottkémek}}), an original shamanic music band.

== Personal worldview ==
From his childhood on he was very interested in dealing with the Sun, the cosmos, music and the nature of life. As an adult he is looking for the answer whether the Universe does have a physical, biological or psychological nature.<ref>Grandpierre 1988, 2002, 2023a,b; Grandpierre, Chopra and Kafatos 2014; Grandpierre, Müller and Elek 2022</ref>

== Life ==
=== Ancestry ===
Grandpierre's family name comes from French [[Huguenot]] ancestors,<ref>{{cite web|title = Fémforgács - Cikk - Vágtázó Életerő|url = http://www.femforgacs.hu/interju/434/Vagtazo_Eletero|website = Femforgacs.hu| date=12 April 2009 |access-date = 2015-06-04}}</ref> according to family tradition, with some French bishops, of whom one, [[Louis Grandpierre]], was a [[Switzerland|Swiss]] politician and president of the Swiss Appeal Court,<ref>{{cite web|title = Grandpierre, Louis|url = http://www.hls-dhs-dss.ch/textes/d/D4515.php|website =Hls-dhs-dss.ch|access-date = 2015-06-08|author= Eric-André}}</ref> and another, [[Károly Grandpierre]], a writer and consultant<ref>A photo of Lajos Kossuth dedicated to Károly Grandpierre. [[c:File:A photo of Lajos Kossuth dedicated to Károly Grandpierre.jpg|wikimedia >>]]
</ref> of [[Lajos Kossuth]], settled in Hungary. 
[[File:Grandpierre Attila 1981-ben.jpg|left|thumb|Attila Grandpierre at age 30 in 1981]]

=== Young years, family ===
Grandpierre was born in Hungary under the Soviet regime on 4 July 1951 in Budapest. His father, [[Endre Grandpierre K.]] was a writer and historian. His father's studies on history greatly influenced the small Attila. He was five years old when he stated that he wanted to become an astronomer, dealing with the Sun, and seven years old when he stated that he wanted to become a singer. He graduated at [[Eötvös Loránd University|ELTE]] as a physicist-astronomer in 1974, and got his Ph.D. in 1977.

==Physicist career==
He studied [[theoretical biology]] focused on [[Ervin Bauer]]'s works. In 2009 his subject field of interest concerned the relation between astronomy and civilization.<ref>{{cite web|title=A. Grandpierre was the main organizer and the Co-chair of the International Scientific Organizing Committee of the conference "Astronomy and Civilization"|date=2009|url=http://www.konkoly.hu/AC2009/|website=Konkoly.hu}}</ref> During 1995-1998 he worked with [[Ervin László|Professor Ervin László]] studying the physics of collective consciousness and the quantum-vacuum interactions.<ref>Grandpierre, A. 1995, Quantum-Vacuum Interactions in the Brain. in the Appendix of The Interconnected Universe. Toward a Unified Science of Quantum, Cosmos and Consciousness, by Ervin Laszlo, ''[[World Scientific]]'', pp. 113-117</ref> In 2011 he was an invited professor on Computational Biology at the [[Chapman University|Chapman University, California]] for six months.

As physicist he had a strong interest in the problem of bringing the sciences and metaphysics together.<ref name=":0" /> He paid special attention to [[Interdisciplinarity|interdisciplinal science]]<ref>A. Grandpierre was the member of the Scientific Board of the International Consortium for Interdisciplinary Science in 2008.</ref> and complexity of living systems in 2008. He paid special attention to comprehensive science unifying the sciences of matter, life and mind, deepening the explanatory structure of sciences [7], complexity of living systems in 2008, the relations between astronomy and civilization in 2011, the living nature of the Sun in 2017, the ancient history of the Silk Road in 2021, and life-centred economics in 2022.

=== Books ===
Grandpierre published 21 books, 7 book chapters, more than 100 science papers, over 400 popular science articles, edited some books.

He wrote the ''Fundamental'' ''Complexity Measures of Life''<ref>{{cite web|title = Fundamental complexity measures of life|url = http://www.konkoly.hu/staff/grandpierre/Complex.htm|website = Konkoly.hu|access-date = 2015-06-02}}</ref> and ''Cosmic Life Forms''<ref>{{cite web|url = http://www.konkoly.hu/staff/grandpierre/Cosmic.pdf|title = Cosmic Life Forms|website=Konkuly.hu }}</ref> chapters in the book titled ''From Fossils to Astrobiology'' (2008, Springer). edited the book Astronomy and Civilization (2011, Analecta Husserliana, [6]), The Helios Theory – The Sun as a Self-Regulating System and as a Cosmic Living Organism (2018, Process Studies,<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Grandpierre |first=Attila |date=2017 |title=The Helios Theory: The Sun as a Self-Regulating System and as a Cosmic Living Organism |url=https://scholarlypublishingcollective.org/ps/article/46/2/206/212057/The-Helios-Theory-The-Sun-as-a-Self-Regulating |journal=Process Studies |language=en |volume=46 |issue=2 |pages=206–228 |doi=10.5406/processstudies.46.2.0206 |issn=0360-6503|url-access=subscription }}</ref> Limits to Growth and the Philosophy of Life-Centred Economics. World Futures (2022, World Futures,<ref name="Grandpierre 2022 440–455">{{Cite journal |last=Grandpierre |first=Attila |date=2022 |title=Limits to Growth and the Philosophy of Life-Centred Economics |url=https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/02604027.2022.2072160 |journal=World Futures |language=en |volume=78 |issue=7 |pages=440–455 |doi=10.1080/02604027.2022.2072160 |issn=0260-4027|url-access=subscription }}</ref> Extending Whiteheadian Organic Cosmology to a Comprehensive Science of Nature (Chapter 2 in Process Cosmology: New Integrations in Science and Philosophy, in the new “Palgrave Perspectives in Process Philosophy”,<ref>{{Cite book |url=https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-3-030-81396-3 |title=Process Cosmology |series=Palgrave Perspectives on Process Philosophy |date=2022 |language=en |doi=10.1007/978-3-030-81396-3|isbn=978-3-030-81395-6 }}</ref> Generalization of Quantum Theory into Biology (book chapter in Process-Philosophical Perspectives on Biology: Intuiting Life,<ref>{{Cite book |url=https://www.cambridgescholars.com/product/978-1-5275-0450-9 |title=Process-Philosophical Perspectives on Biology: Intuiting Life |isbn=978-1-5275-0450-9 |series=European Studies in Process Thought |last1=Koutroufinis |first1=Spyridon A. |last2=Araujo |first2=Arthur |date=2023 }}</ref> wrote two chapters and edited “The Cosmic Life Instinct Shows the Way for the Healthy Civilization” (2023, Springer,<ref>{{Cite book |url=https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-981-99-2131-7 |title=Towards a Philosophy of Cosmic Life |date=2023 |language=en |doi=10.1007/978-981-99-2131-7 |isbn=978-981-99-2130-0 |editor-last1=Bartosch |editor-last2=Grandpierre |editor-last3=Peng |editor-first1=David |editor-first2=Attila |editor-first3=Bei }}</ref>).

He was co-editor of the book ''Astronomy and Civilization in the New Enlightenment'' (2011, Springer).<ref name=":0">{{Cite book|title = Astronomy and Civilization in the New Enlightenment - Passions of the Skies |publisher=Springer.com|url = https://www.springer.com/us/book/9789048197477#aboutBook}}</ref>

=== Important publications ===
In astrophysics he wrote an article on the variable nature of the Sun's core, which was mentioned in New Scientist as giving the best fit to explain the periodicities of terrestrial Ice Ages<ref>{{cite magazine|last=Clark |first=Stuart |url=https://www.newscientist.com/article/mg19325884.500-suns-fickle-heart-may-leave-us-cold.html |title=Sun's fickle heart may leave us cold |magazine=[[New Scientist]] |date=2007-01-24 |access-date=2020-04-07}}</ref> in 2007.

Working with Katalin Martinás, he wrote on "natural" thermodynamics.<ref>Martinas, K. and Grandpierre, A. 2009, Natural Thermodynamics. Kopenhagen, June 22–24, 2009, Conceptual Thermodynamics, The Joint European Thermodynamics Conference, Copenhagen {{cite web|url=http://www.jetc10.fys.ku.dk/?q%3Dconceptual |title=Conceptual thermodynamics &#124; jetc10.fys.ku.dk |access-date=2015-06-01 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150602172155/http://www.jetc10.fys.ku.dk/?q=conceptual |archive-date=2015-06-02 }}</ref> Since 2020, he is the Research President of the Budapest Centre for Long-Term Sustainability.

He generalised the principle of least action, playing a fundamental role in physics, to the principle of biology as the principle of greatest action.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.cambridgescholars.com/product/978-1-5275-0450-9 | title=Process-Philosophical Perspectives on Biology: Intuiting Life - Cambridge Scholars Publishing }}</ref>

== Musician career ==
{{Main|Galloping Coroners|Galloping Wonder Stag}} As a musician Atilla Grandpierre is best known as leader/vocalist of Galloping Coroners (Vágtázó Halottkémek in Hungarian, Die Rasenden Leichenbeschauer in German, where they were a cultic band in the 80’s and 90’s) shamanic band inspired by the cosmic life force, from 1975-today and later also the same of acoustic Galloping Wonder Stag from 2005-today.

By his high school years, before he had started to sing, he had countrywide fame among youngsters as a boy who did crazy things with his friends; e.g. creating homemade rockets.<ref>{{cite web|title = Interjú Grandpierre Atillával |website=Grandpierre.hu|date=23 October 2008 |url = http://www.grandpierre.hu/site/2008/10/interju-grandpierre-atillaval/|access-date = 2015-06-08}}</ref>
